clue.text: When Ken gets stuck into the weeds?

definitions.text: When Ken gets stuck into the weeds?

indicators.note: something stuck into another thing is pushed inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, a man's name

explanation.surface: A gardener called Ken finally gets round to tackling the weedy patch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole clue: Saturdays and Sundays are when a weekend gardener like Ken gets round to attacking the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday and Sunday are the days off when most people find time for gardening chores.

clue.text: A brief era of famine

parts.note: brief means short
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A short historical period remembered for famine.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is a severe lack of food, a dearth or scarcity.

clue.text: Maximum speed permitted for the A1

definitions.text: Maximum speed permitted for the A1

parts.words: Maximum speed permitted for the A1
parts.note: reads like the speed limit on Britain's A1 road, but A1 also means first-class, and the highest band of tax or pay is the phrase wanted

explanation.surface: A question about the speed limit on the A1, the main road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; 'A1' also means excellent, and a maximum rate of pay or tax is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest band of charge or tax is its uppermost level, the most anyone pays.

clue.text: Turkish leader about to conclude business of the meeting

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the leader's title wraps round the other word

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish chief or commander
to conclude is to end

explanation.surface: A Turkish chief is about to wrap up the items for discussion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting's business is set out in its list of items to discuss.

clue.text: Bogside soldiers in service

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Bogside soldiers in service': wordplay is OR inside MASS, and the definition must be 'Bog', but it is fused with 'side' in one word, leaving 'side' with no job.

clue.text: Can an X-ray machine perceive a man's true purpose?

definitions.text: Can an X-ray machine perceive a man's true purpose?

parts.words: Can an X-ray machine perceive a man's true purpose?
parts.note: an X-ray machine literally looks right through a person's body, and the idiom means detecting someone's hidden motives

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a hospital scanner could reveal what a person really intends.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means recognising a person's deceit or real motives despite their pretence.

clue.text: Hurtful stabs following bullet wounds

definitions.meaning: sudden darting pangs of pain
literally, the pains that come after being shot

explanation.definitionFit: Sharp sudden pangs that seem to dart through the body are described with a gunfire metaphor.

clue.text: Go on a stable diet or have a nosh-up

definitions.meaning: eat as a stabled animal does, on hay and oats
a nosh-up is British slang for a big hearty meal

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to eat enormous quantities, like a hungry horse in its stable.

clue.text: An outstanding device for sealing wine bottles

definitions.meaning: an outstanding thing or person, an excellent example
a machine that pushes stoppers into bottles

explanation.definitionFit: Informally a splendid person or thing is a cracker; literally, a machine that inserts stoppers.

clue.text: In children tact serves to protect tenants' rights

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of these clue words, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: Teaching children diplomacy is said to help those who rent their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'children' through 'tact' into the start of 'serves'; the definition describes the laws by their purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: These are British statutes passed to safeguard people who lease their homes from landlords.

clue.text: Scottish pair using international airline

definitions.meaning: the Scots word for two
Trans World Airlines, the former American carrier

explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect for two, and the initials of Trans World Airlines.

clue.text: Way a New Zealand article portrays a piece of poetry

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Kiwi street scene is depicted in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Thin spar adapted to move cargo to another vessel

indicators.note: adapted means altered or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slender pole is modified to help shift freight between boats.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer goods from one boat to another at sea or in port.

clue.text: Manila's centre yields nothing

indicators.note: the centre of the city name holds the letters wanted, taken from inside it

explanation.surface: The middle of the Philippine capital produces nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first two and last letters of MANILA (MA and A) to leave its central run.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero, a score of none, as in football results.

clue.text: Worked up how to cook tough meat

definitions.meaning: agitated, flustered
slow simmering in liquid tenderises tough cuts

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means anxious or flustered; literally, simmering in a pot as a casserole.

clue.text: Where a shoe comes to a point

definitions.text: Where a shoe comes to a point

parts.words: Where a shoe comes to a point
parts.note: the pointed front end of a shoe, where it narrows

explanation.surface: A description of the narrow front end of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The front tip of a shoe covers the digits of the foot.

clue.text: Spread out for single hit by a batsman

parts.note: in cricket a batsman plays a ball by striking it

explanation.surface: A cricket shot for one run sends the fielders scattering.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is one run, which tempts the solver toward a run abbreviation; here it gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Splayed limbs or fingers are spread wide apart.

clue.text: Stage at which train passengers alight

definitions.meaning: a raised floor for speakers or performers
the raised area beside the track at a station

explanation.definitionFit: A raised floor serves both as a stage for speakers and as the station area beside the rails.

clue.text: For a cricketer to get one run is a shambles

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring a single run is laughed at as a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shambles' means a mess, but its old sense is a slaughterhouse, which is the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse, where animals are killed.

clue.text: Smouldering anger

definitions.meaning: burning slowly, as aromatic sticks and resin do
to anger is to enrage

explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant resin or sticks burn slowly with sweet smoke; as a verb it means to enrage.

clue.text: An extra plea of clemency for murderer

definitions.meaning: a substitute player or reserve, one more than needed
a plea to let the guilty fellow live, phrased as an imperative

explanation.definitionFit: A reserve person kept in hand; and a cry to show mercy to the killer.

clue.text: Truly a way to make a second marriage

definitions.meaning: genuinely, in fact

definitions.text: a way to make a second marriage
definitions.meaning: to join again in alliance, wedding anew

explanation.definitionFit: Means genuinely; split with a hyphen, it is to form an alliance anew.

clue.text: Sheepish type doctor going around Ireland

indicators.note: going around means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A doctor travels around Ireland, looking rather embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' suggests embarrassment, but here it means a kind of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of sheep prized for its fine wool, originally from Spain.

clue.text: In pain father must be brave

indicators.note: in means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: an ache is a pain
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad who is hurting must show courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and this people are a famous tribe.

clue.text: Bed suitable for a small house

definitions.meaning: a child's bed with high sides
a cottage, especially in poetry

explanation.definitionFit: A baby's sleeping place; also a poetic word for a humble cottage.

clue.text: One old prisoner is employed in priceless metalwork

indicators.note: employed in means placed within, so the pieces go inside the other word

parts.note: priceless taken as costing nothing, free
I is the Roman numeral one
a lag is an old convict

explanation.surface: A veteran convict is set to work making expensive ornamental metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless' suggests very valuable, but here it means costing nothing. FILAGREE is a variant spelling of the more usual filigree.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate ornamental work of fine twisted wire, usually gold or silver.

clue.text: A tense time ahead

definitions.meaning: a grammatical verb tense, as in 'will go'
the period yet to come

explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical tense for events to come, and the period still to come.

clue.text: Submarines' vigil

definitions.meaning: the submarine arm of a navy, so called for its stealth
a watch or devotion kept without speaking

explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for the navy's undersea fleet, and a quiet watch or worship.
